contentBlocks.text: This week you built a real toolkit for analyzing HOW authors write, not just WHAT they write. Let's review it all together.

Quick review: word choice creates tone (Day 1). Similes and metaphors compare unlike things to create vivid meaning (Day 2). Sensory imagery pulls readers into a scene using the five senses (Day 3). All of these craft choices serve the author's purpose — to inform, persuade, or entertain (Day 4). Read this sentence: 'The old dog moved like a rusty machine, each step creaking with the weight of years.' Identify the tone, any figurative language, any sensory imagery, and the likely author's purpose.
Excellent work this week — you now have a complete toolkit for analyzing an author's craft that you'll apply to every text you read going forward.

objectives: Recall all four craft-analysis elements: tone, figurative language, sensory imagery, author's purpose
Apply all four elements to analyze one new sentence
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Work through the 'old dog' sentence analysis together, identifying all 4 elements.
3. Complete the cumulative review worksheet.
4. Discuss any mismatches or uncertain answers together before finishing.
5. Celebrate finishing the first full week of this unit — this same 4-part analysis will apply to every text studied this year.
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow the child to use their Day 1-4 worksheets as a reference during review rather than working from memory alone
Ready for more: ask them to rewrite the 'old dog' sentence with a completely different tone (playful instead of weary) while keeping the same basic fact
This is a good checkpoint to note which day's concept needs the most re-teaching before moving to next week's unit
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. Tone: weary/tired, evoking age and slowness. 2. Figurative language: simile ('like a rusty machine'). 3. Sensory imagery: 'creaking' appeals to sound. 4. Purpose: likely to entertain, creating vivid, emotional imagery rather than just stating a fact.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates the week's Common Core Grade 7 Reading standards (RL.7.4, RI.7.6) into one complete craft analysis, matching the course's own 'analyzing an author's craft' description end to end.

Identify the figurative language (simile or metaphor).
